newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian government warns farmers of food shortage.
newsitem.headline: Zambian government warns farmers of food shortage.

text.p: The Zambian government on Tuesday warned farmers against selling all their harvests as production of maize and other major food crops had fallen markedly this year.
Agriculture Minister Edith Nawakwi said in a statement that excessive rains and inadequate fertiliser supplies had led to a maize shortfall of 272,000 tonnes.

"Our national maize requirement stands at 1,363,000 metric tons. From our production and carryover stocks, about 1,090,000 metric tons will be available, implying a shortfall of about 272,000 tons," Nawakwi said.

"Let me advise farmers who are in the habit of selling all of their crop output that, in view of the expected shortfall of food crops...watch your food quantities and retain enough cereals for your own consumption," she added.
Maize production fell by 32 percent from 15.7 million to 10.7 million 90 kg (198 lb) bags.
Nawakwi said sorghum output fell by nearly 14 percent to 341,734 90 kg bags from 396,005 90 kg bags while sunflower production fell to 159,664 bags from 535,715 bags.
Soyabean production went down by 27 percent to 325,462 bags from 445,001 bags. Paddy rice and mixed beans production went down by six and 45 percent respectively.
However, production of groundnuts and millet rose by 44 and 11 percent respectively.
Nawakwi said the government would not import food to meet the shortfall.
"The deficits in maize and other food crops...are expected to be met by the private sector," she said.

"We have a liberalised economy with the government not participating in agricultural marketing. The private sector should be actively involved in sourcing whatever commodity is lacking in the country and make it their business," she added.
